findings.title: Protocol promises cross Ready, durability, and recovery boundaries
findings.summary: This code-review scenario concerns the boundary between volatile Raft decisions, captured Ready batches, caller durability, and recovered state. The brief notes that sends are only queued, Ready can contain both committed and unstable work, Advance acknowledges captured endpoints, and RawNode uses an empty-log new-node inference after loading saved state. Confirmation should determine whether permitted persistence, publication, application, Advance, crash, and restart interleavings can expose promises or recovery obligations without valid durable backing.

findings.title: Election and transfer eligibility depend on local configuration progress
findings.summary: This code-review scenario concerns election, PreVote, vote-grant, vote-counting, and leadership-transfer paths observing local configuration progress at different times. The brief cites different guards for Hup, TimeoutNow, transfer campaigns, learner vote grants, and PreVote continuation into campaign. Confirmation should determine whether configuration lag across events can produce incorrect eligibility, history safety, or management-progress outcomes.

findings.title: Released application work and effective membership are different state
findings.summary: This code-review scenario concerns the gap between released application work, Raft's applied cursor, and the configuration that is effective only after the application callback. The brief notes that Advance may precede application, pending-conf admission consults the applied cursor, and membership changes take effect separately from committed or released entries. Confirmation should determine whether delayed configuration application, restart replay suppression, promotion, demotion, or removal can violate configuration-transition or election assumptions.

findings.title: Replication evidence and snapshot boundaries change at different times
findings.summary: This code-review scenario concerns Match, Next, inflight quota, volatile and stable log suffixes, snapshots, and application cursors moving on different schedules. The brief cites state-dependent rejection guards, heartbeat quota release without Match advancement, separate snapshot status paths, and full restore movement of first index and commit without moving applied. Confirmation should determine whether these interleavings can break replication evidence, snapshot backing, catch-up, or legal scheduling expectations.

findings.title: ReadIndex evidence must survive membership and application interleavings
findings.summary: This code-review scenario concerns ReadIndex initiation, leadership confirmation, captured commit index, queue-prefix release, delivery, and actual read response observing different membership and application states. The brief cites the current-term gate, heartbeat-ack quorum evaluation, queued-context release, count-only singleton checks, and self-removal behavior without a matching ReadIndex guard. Confirmation should determine whether completed reads can lack a valid leadership, commit, membership, request-correlation, or applied-prefix basis.

findings.title: Admission, rejection, cancellation, and retry are protocol outcomes
findings.summary: This code-review scenario concerns API handoff, internal acceptance, rejection, cancellation, retry, and completion signals as distinct protocol outcomes. The brief notes differences between Node and RawNode result paths, proposal waiting under no-leader conditions, pending-conf bookkeeping, quota release, and read-state clearing. Confirmation should determine whether these wrapper and admission outcomes are soundly represented and whether any legal call sequence produces an incorrect success, rejection, cancellation, or retry obligation.
